title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, arena tuning
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Reduce GPU peak memory by enabling selective activation checkpointing, pooling transient scratch buffers, and tuning allocator arena sizes. Expected to reduce OOMs for long-sequence workloads and increase effective batch capacity. Minor latency impact for some long-sequence configs.
description: Motivation: Long-sequence generation and large-batch inference on constrained GPU memory (A100 40GB, RTX-class cards) hit OOMs and require customers to reduce batch size or sequence length. This PR reduces transient workspace and peak activation memory via three orthogonal changes: (1) selective activation checkpointing hooks so we can checkpoint expensive FFN/attention subgraphs without global model changes; (2) a transient scratch buffer pool (thread-safe, per-stream) to avoid repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree and to share short-lived temporary workspace across kernels; (3) allocator arena/limit tuning to reduce reserved workspace per-stream and bound fragmentation on multi-model/multi-stream usage. This description summarizes the work, testing, and review thread in a single continuous string. Changes are scoped to the runtime and a small set of kernel optimizations; interface changes are internal and backwards compatible. Microbench results in this PR show ~15-22% peak GPU memory reduction across long-sequence workloads with a 2-5% median latency regression for worst-case configs, and no throughput regression when continuous batching is enabled.
commit_summary: core/runtime: add selective activation checkpointing hooks + config flag (enable_checkpointing_per_layer)
core/runtime: introduce transient scratch buffer pool (scratch_pool.{cc,hh}) with per-stream free-lists and stats
core/runtime/allocator: tune default arena sizes, reduce max-reserved workspace per-stream, add fragmentation metrics
kernels/attention: reduce temporary workspace by reusing preallocated scratch segments on SM80 and SM90 paths
bench: add long-sequence memory regression bench and CI job
docs: add perf/arena_tuning.md and migration notes for Dedicated customers
perf_results: A100-40GB, seq=8192 batch=1: peak GPU memory -18% (from 33.2GB to 27.2GB), p50 latency +2.4%
RTX6000, seq=4096 batch=4: peak GPU memory -22% (from 28.1GB to 21.9GB), p50 latency +3.8%
Dedicated small GPU (16GB), seq=2048 batch=2: enabled checkpointing allowed same batch where OOM occurred previously
Continuous batching enabled: throughput unchanged or slightly improved (+1-2%) because reduced memory allows more concurrent requests
